title: Release Corridor Governor: declarative rollout lanes, weight curators, and safety envelopes
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Build a canonical policy engine for 'release corridors' that expresses declarative rollout lanes (traffic weight schedules, shadow lanes, and A/B cohorts), automatically enforces guardrails, and triggers automated rollback when safety envelopes are violated. This engine should be usable from the Redwood Console and via the API, support hosted/dedicated/private deployments, and integrate with existing telemetry and alerting. The goal is predictable, auditable rollouts that minimize blast radius while allowing staged exposure for model variants across regions and customer tiers.
acceptance_criteria: API and Console controls to create a rollout policy that specifies ordered steps with explicit traffic percentages and durations
Runtime enforces guardrails: error-rate, p95 latency, throughput SLOs, and custom business metrics; violations pause progression and can trigger rollback rules
Support for shadow lanes (mirror X% of traffic) without affecting user experience and with observability hooks into the evaluation pipeline
Dry-run / simulation mode that predicts traffic distribution and estimates cost uplift and latency impact before activating
End-to-end integration test proving canary progression, pause-on-violation, and automatic rollback in a staging environment
Audit log entries for every decision (step advance, pause, rollback) with reason codes and metric snapshots
tasks: Design DSL for rollout policies (steps, targets, matchers, tolerances)
Implement policy compiler that translates DSL to runtime routing rules
Add guardrail evaluator service: ingest metrics, evaluate thresholds, emit decision events
Integrate with Router to apply fractional traffic and shadow mirroring
Expose Console UI for policy authoring and live timeline visualization
Create simulation harness and cost estimator for proposed policies
Author integration tests and chaos scenarios for rollback validation
Prepare migration script for existing rollout objects to new schema
design_decisions: Choose declarative JSON/YAML DSL vs imperative API: we pick declarative DSL to make policies auditable and human-reviewable
Policy evaluation model: evaluate at fixed intervals (10s) rather than per-request to reduce decision churn
Guardrail evaluation source: primary signal is realtime metrics from telemetry pipeline; secondary signal is sampled request traces for anomaly confirmation
Rollback semantics: two tiers - soft-pause (manual review required) and hard-rollback (automated when critical thresholds exceeded)
Traffic enforcement: use token-stealing continuous-batcher-friendly weights rather than per-request hashing to reduce latency variance
implementation_notes: Policy DSL fields: id, name, matchers, steps[{duration, percent}], shadow_percent, guardrails[{metric, window, threshold, comparator, severity}], actions[{on_violation}]
Compiler output: ordered routing intents + constraint set for guardrail service
Persist policies in config-store (etcd-backed) with versioned schema and migration hooks
Guardrail evaluator runs as sidecar-able service; publishes decision events to event-bus (Kafka) and writes audit records
Router integration: accept signed routing-intent token for enforcement; support per-tenant overrides for Dedicated tenants
API rate-limits for policy changes and safety checks to avoid thrashing in high churn
telemetry_requirements: Emit per-policy metric streams: active_users, request_count, error_rate, p95_latency, cost_per_token
Attach tags: policy_id, step_index, variant_id, region, tenant_id
Expose decision_events metric for console timeline (advance/pause/rollback with timestamp and reason)
Retention: 90 days for policy metrics; 365 days for audit logs for enterprise customers
rollout_plan: Week 1: finalise DSL and compile model; unit tests for compiler
Week 2: implement guardrail evaluator and basic Router integration; local staging validation
Week 3: Console UI PoC and simulation mode; run internal dogfood canaries with low traffic
Week 4: end-to-end integration tests and chaos scenarios (network partitions, metrics delay)
Week 5: soft launch on canary customers, monitor, then enable auto-rollback for critical policies
risks_and_mitigations: Metric lag causing false positives: mitigate by using multiple windows and confirmation sampling before hard-rollback
Complexity of DSL leading to misconfiguration: provide strong validation, lints and default safety profiles
Performance overhead in Router: implement lightweight enforcement token and perform weight calculations in routing-layer C++ hot path
Cross-region consistency issues: versioned policy evaluation and region-local guardrail thresholds to avoid cascading rollbacks
